68.0.s.en: (1) The joy of the righteous in God the Victor

68.0.0.en: 1- Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.

68.0.1.en: 1- Moses used to recite this verse when the ark of the covenant of God and the tabernacle of meeting were moved from one place to another in the wilderness of Sinai, declaring the power of God, in whom His people believe, and of whom His enemies are afraid, who did not believe in Him but know His power, chiefly the demons, the pagan gods, and the peoples who follow them.

68.0.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ, who rises from the dead on the third day, binding Satan, and it is also a prophecy about the second resurrection and the day of judgment, when those who hate God hide from His face (Rev 6:16).

68.1.0.en: 2- As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

68.1.1.en: 3- But let the righteous be glad; let them rejoice before God: yea, let them exceedingly rejoice.

68.1.4.en: 1- The wicked have no power before God, and by the wicked are meant the demons and all who follow them. He likens them to smoke that the winds disperse, or to chaff that is tossed and flies in the air, away from the grains of wheat. So the smoke is not found and the chaff is scattered.

68.1.5.en: 2- He also likens the wicked to wax that melts with the heat of fire, and even flies away so that it is not found. Fire signifies the work of the Holy Spirit, who burns sins out of a person so that he is purified; this is for the righteous, but as for the wicked, or the demons, all their works are burned by the fire of the Holy Spirit and are not found.

68.1.6.en: 3- When the righteous see the power of God that scatters the wicked and their works (which He likened to the divine wind and the fire that at the same time purify the righteous), they rejoice, and with the purity of their hearts they behold God, so their gladness increases, and indeed their feelings are stirred, and they leap, rejoicing and praising God for His power and His great works with them, and how He protects them from the evils around them.

68.2.0.en: 4- Sing unto God, sing praises to his name; prepare a way for him that rideth through the deserts by his name Yah, and rejoice before him. Deserts: wastelands in which there is no water, nor plants, nor man.

68.2.1.en: Yah: short for Yahweh, which is the name of God.

68.2.2.en: 1- The prophet David calls on the children of God to shout His name, and perhaps he was bringing the ark of the covenant of God from the house of Obed-edom the Gittite; for God rides in His ark of the covenant after it had been a stranger among the Gentile Philistines, and now returns by the hand of David to Jerusalem, His holy city. His being among the Gentiles is signified by the deserts, but His being among His children is thus within the good land, where His children sprout and bear good fruit, and His name Yahweh is clear and proclaimed among His people; therefore they prepare His way with shouting and glorifying, so they rejoice and make the heart of God rejoice.

68.2.3.en: 2- God who rides and comes from the deserts is Christ incarnate, who declared the holy name of God; for no one has seen God, but the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared Him (Jn 1:18); therefore the angels shouted, and the believing children of God such as the Virgin, for His great Incarnation.

68.3.0.en: 5- A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.

68.3.1.en: 1- When a person is far from God he is like the orphan, that is, one without a father, and like the widow, that is, one without a husband and support; but by faith a person acquires God within himself, and God sanctifies him and dwells in him, so the person becomes the holy dwelling of God, that is, God cares for His weak children who need Him, so He satisfies them, lifts them up and sanctifies them, and they are higher than the whole world, because He dwells in them, after He has saved them from Satan who controlled them when they worshiped idols or were immersed in lusts, and He changed them from orphans into believers proud of their Father, and from widows into His bride.

68.3.2.en: 2- God's holy dwelling is also Jerusalem where the ark of the covenant of God was, and it is also His Incarnation in the fullness of time, and likewise it is the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom, in addition to the human soul in which God dwells, as we mentioned before.

68.4.0.en: 6- God setteth the solitary in a house; he bringeth out those which are bound to prosperity: but the rebellious dwell in a scorched land.

68.4.2.en: Scorched land: land that is dry and hot from the intensity of the sun's heat.

68.4.3.en: 1- The solitary are those who have no one to care for them, and who are separated from others, and by them He means His people the Jews, who separated from the world and worshiped God, so He settles them in His house and dwells in their midst. The solitary are also the orphans and widows, and every person who suffers weakness, whom God cares for, giving him stability and even distinction, as he is settled in God's hands. And everyone who was enslaved to sin and became its captive God frees, as long as he has believed in Him and repented, and gives him success in his life.

68.4.4.en: 2- On the other hand, those who rebel against God and reject His commandments and faith and life with Him, God keeps in Gehenna and eternal torment, where the fire is not quenched, and they are completely deprived of seeing God and enjoying Him.

68.4.5.en: The sweet God is available to you to enjoy the sight of Him and fellowship with Him, so do not be distracted from Him, and know that your sins that separate you from Him you can be rid of through repentance, however much they have mastered you. Trust that He will help you and free you from your sins, and even make you succeed in all your steps, and give you inner stability, and you will delight in being with Him.

68.5.s.en: (2) Crossing the wilderness and entering Canaan

68.5.0.en: 7- O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people, when thou didst ascend in the wilderness; Selah.

68.5.1.en: 1- David tells us about God's going forth before His people to free them from the slavery of Egypt: He walked before them in a pillar of cloud by day to shade them from the heat of the sun, and in a pillar of fire by night to light the way for them, and He crossed the Red Sea, and walked with them in the barren wilderness, that is, Sinai; He fed them, gave them water and kept them until He brought them to the land of Canaan. And God continued to go forth before His people through His great works with them, and He still does so to this day.

68.5.2.en: 2- Christ went forth before His Church and crossed with her from death to life by His cross, and after His resurrection ascended into the heavens, rising above the wilderness of this world. And everyone who believes in Christ sees Him as his leader in the world, until He brings him up into the heavens. God appears to His children who believe in Him, and not to the whole world. The people of God of old, and the Church today, enjoyed God's care and leadership; even if their appearance is one of distress, they are in truth victorious and joyful because of Christ's presence in their midst.

68.5.3.en: 3- If God goes forth before His people of the children of Israel, He also goes forth before the Gentiles, who are signified by the wilderness because they were far from faith; when they believe, faith lifts them up to a lofty life with God, then to glories in heaven, so the believers, whether of the Jews or of the Gentiles, are one in Christ, and ascend through Him to the glories of heaven.

68.5.4.en: 4- He closes the verse with the word "Selah," which is a musical pause for meditating on God, who leads His people and leads your life to keep you and care for you.

68.6.0.en: 8- The earth shook, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God: even Sinai itself was moved at the presence of God, the God of Israel.

68.6.1.en: 1- When God appeared on the mountain with smoke, mist, thunder and fire, the earth quaked, and the wilderness of Sinai, "Sinai itself," quaked, and the heavens dropped with the Ten Commandments, the Law of God, and the design of the tabernacle of meeting; for God appeared to declare His power and love and His readiness to dwell in the midst of His people, and to give them His commandments and Law, that they might live by them.

68.6.2.en: 2- At the crucifixion of Christ the earth quaked and the rocks were split, and after His resurrection many of those who slept came out, that is, the heavens dropped, and some lofty spirits of the saints came and entered their bodies and appeared after the resurrection of Christ, to confirm His resurrection and call people to faith. The redemption of Christ shook the kingdom of Satan, that is, all the powers of Satan do not stand before the believer in Christ, but shake before him.

68.7.0.en: 9- Thou, O God, didst pour out a plentiful rain; thine inheritance, when it was weary, thou didst restore.

68.7.2.en: 1- The plentiful rain that He granted to His people in the wilderness of Sinai is the manna and the quail, and also His commandments and His Law. And when He found sins in His people, who are His inheritance, such as murmuring, He restored them by His grace and purified them, so all the murmurers died in the wilderness of Sinai, and only His innocent children entered the land of Canaan.

68.7.3.en: 2- The prophet David says to God that his inheritance is from God, that is, the people of God, whom David shepherded faithfully, but David declares with humility that he is a sinner and weak, and was not able to shepherd the people of God perfectly, but the tender God intervened and repaired the results of David's mistakes. David sinned by adultery and murder, but God made him repent at the hand of Nathan, and he sinned by numbering the people, but God punished him and punished the people, and he and his people returned to God with repentance.

68.7.4.en: 3- The plentiful rain is also the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church, "thine inheritance," and God's restoring of His people by means of convicting them by the Holy Spirit, repentance and confession, and every Church discipline, in addition to partaking of the Holy Mysteries. Thus God's special care for His people appears because of their submission to Him. For God pours out many gifts, which are like the plentiful rain, upon everyone who loves Him and clings to Him.

68.8.0.en: 10- Thy congregation hath dwelt therein: thou, O God, hast prepared of thy goodness for the poor.

68.8.1.en: 1- David continues his discourse about the people of God, describing them as God's flock, and He is their faithful Shepherd, so He settled them in the wilderness of Sinai, where it is difficult for a human being to dwell, and even fed them, gave them water, kept them in their wars, and delivered them from all the hardships of the wilderness, because they are His people, and He is responsible for them.

68.9.0.en: 11- The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.

68.9.1.en: 1- God gave His Law and His commandments to Moses by angels, and Moses preached and taught them to his people through the priests and the Levites, who are also the great host.

68.9.2.en: 2- In the New Testament God gave His Word to humanity, which is the Incarnation of Christ, and accomplished the redemption of humanity on the cross, and the "great host" proclaimed the salvation of Christ, who are the Apostles and priests and all the servants of the New Testament.

68.10.0.en: 12- Kings of armies did flee, did flee: and she that tarried at home divided the spoil.

68.10.1.en: 1- The children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai, and then in the land of Canaan, were exposed to facing trained armies led by kings, whereas the children of Israel were not trained for war, and by the power of God they defeated the enemies, who fled before them, and the children of Israel took their spoil, which was very great, and it was not divided only among the fighting men of the children of Israel, but they also gave to the women, and to all the sick and the old who stayed at home because of their inability to fight, so each one took his share of the enemies' spoil.

68.10.2.en: 2- God gives His children victory over the armies of the demons and their chiefs, so the demons flee before them, and the children of God take much spoil from the hand of God, which is virtues and the fruits of the Holy Spirit, and everyone who stays at home, that is, the Church, receives it. And in the end, after this life, God's holy children take the spoil of the demons, as they reign in their place in the heavens.

68.11.0.en: 13- Though ye have lien among the sheepfolds, yet shall ye be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold.

68.11.1.en: 1- Lying among the sheepfolds means taking possession of the promised land which God promised to the fathers, and Joshua divided it among the tribes of the children of Israel; so when you possess the land you enjoy a life with God, simple and innocent like the dove. You need to be committed to the word of God and His commandments, which silver signifies, and you are like gold which signifies heaven, that is, you have heavenly spiritual longings.

68.11.2.en: 2- Lying among the sheepfolds signifies settling in the Church, the house of God, and being nourished by the word of God, in addition to enjoying the blessings of redemption, all this is signified by silver, and your life is lifted up in longing for eternity and the Kingdom of Heaven. In addition, the dove returns to its home, as Noah's dove did when it returned to him, and this signifies the souls which, when they go out into the world, must return to the Church, their home, where they settle with God.

68.12.0.en: 14- When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was white as snow in Salmon.

68.12.1.en: Salmon: one of the peaks of Mount Gerizim, which lies beside Shechem, south of Samaria, among the northern tribes of Israel.

68.12.2.en: 1- If God settled His people and gave them the enjoyment of the land of Canaan, on the other hand He scattered the pagan kings who dwelt in the land of old, that is, God triumphed over these kings and drove them out of their lands.

68.12.3.en: 2- Mount Salmon is known in the land of Canaan as a dark and gloomy mountain, and this signifies the dark pagan life of the peoples who dwelt in the land of Canaan. This mountain God clothed with snow, so it became white and beautiful, a symbol of the pure life of the people of God who dwelt in the land of Canaan, of whom we spoke in the preceding verses, over whom the silver and golden dove hovers, with the spiritual meanings we explained.

68.12.4.en: 3- Christ by His cross transferred humanity from the life of darkness, which Mount Salmon signifies, to the pure, enlightened life, which the snow that covered the mountain, especially its peaks, signifies.

68.12.5.en: If only your stability were in the Church, so that you come to her often to cast all your burdens and troubles on God in her, and enjoy seeing Him; this will encourage you to pray at all times and to walk in His commandments.

68.13.s.en: (3) Dwelling in Zion, and ascending to heaven

68.13.0.en: 15- The hill of God is as the hill of Bashan; a humped hill is the hill of Bashan. 16- Why look ye with envy, ye humped hills, at the hill which God desired for his dwelling? yea, the Lord will dwell in it for ever.

68.13.1.en: Bashan: a very fertile region lying east of the river Jordan, in which there is much cultivation and animals full of fatness.

68.13.2.en: Humped: from hump, the triangular protuberance on the back of the camel, which is full of fat.

68.13.3.en: 1- David addresses the mountains of the fertile region of Bashan, each of which has several peaks resembling the humps of camels full of fat, like the abundant animals and crops of Bashan. And he says to these great mountains full of greenery and richness: Why do you watch Mount Zion on which the city of Jerusalem is built, in which is the ark of the covenant of God, and after this the temple of Solomon? For the mountain of God, the mountain of Bashan, which God filled with richness and greenery, looks at a small mountain, Mount Zion, and counts it blessed because it received the blessing of God's dwelling by the presence of the house of the Lord in it.

68.13.4.en: 2- Mount Bashan signifies the Gentiles who entered into faith, and look to Jerusalem, built on Mount Zion, and see their salvation through Christ incarnate for the redemption of humanity.

68.13.5.en: 3- If high mountains that God endowed with richness like Bashan admire the greatness of little Mount Zion, because it is distinguished by God's presence in it, then it is not right for the people of God to sacrifice in any place other than the house of the Lord, as many erred at different times and sacrificed on mountains that were not the mountain of God.

68.13.6.en: 4- The mountains of the world are rich and great, but the Church of God, that is, His house, even if she seems small, like Mount Zion, is greater than any place in the world because God dwells in her, not only in this world, but after the passing away of heaven and earth He remains dwelling in her, that is, in the Kingdom of Heaven, where the triumphant Church is.

68.14.0.en: 17- The chariots of God are ten thousands, thousands upon thousands: the Lord is among them, Sinai is in the sanctuary.

68.14.1.en: Ten thousands: plural of ten thousand.

68.14.2.en: 1- David shows the greatness of God, whose glory appears among His angels who carry His throne. He shows that their numbers are very great, for they are thousands of thousands and ten thousands of ten thousands, as he says they are repeated, meaning millions of millions, all these angels praise God and glorify Him. And as God reigns over His angels, His reign is also repeated over everyone of mankind who believes in Him.

68.14.3.en: 2- If God is surrounded by myriads of His angels in heaven, He also appeared among His people at Sinai, and dwelt in the tabernacle of meeting, which He sanctified for Himself, and continued to sanctify the temple of Solomon and the city of Jerusalem; for He works in all generations, as He worked with His people by the crossing of the sea, the manna and quail, and the water from the rock. And He sanctifies His Church throughout time, and every human soul that believes in Him and loves Him and submits to Him, so that His kingdom may be in heaven among His angels, and on earth He dwells in His children who believe in Him.

68.15.0.en: 18- Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts among men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the Lord God might dwell among them.

68.15.1.en: 1- In this verse David prophesies about Christ, who rose from the dead and ascended into the heavens, and brought up those who believe in Him who were in Hades, and brought them into Paradise, that is, the souls that were under the authority of the devil He freed, and they became His followers, for He bought them with His blood, so they became servants to Him, and He took them captive by His love. These captives are the gifts that Christ the Son received from the Father, and some of these souls were rebellious against God and walked in evil for a time, but they believed in Christ, and became a dwelling for God, and St. Paul the Apostle quoted this verse in (Eph 4:8).

68.15.2.en: 2- Christ in His Incarnation humbled Himself and received gifts from people, such as the gifts of the Magi, and those who used to put money in the box that Judas Iscariot kept, to provide for the needs of Christ and His disciples, and Mary the mother of Mark, who hosted Christ in her house in the upper room, and those who gave the colt and the donkey to Christ; for He received gifts from them to encourage them to give, and He gave them life by His redemption, which is the greatest gift.

68.15.3.en: Christ ascended to heaven in order to raise you in Him to the glories, so remember that you are a stranger on earth and your place is in heaven, that you may keep away from every sin and live a spiritual, heavenly life.

68.16.0.en: 19- Blessed be the Lord, who day by day bears us up, even the God of our salvation. Selah.

68.16.1.en: 1- God's care for His children appears in that He carries them throughout their lives in His hands, that is, He keeps them, provides for their needs, and cares for them; not only material care, but rather spiritual care, that is, He is concerned for the salvation of their souls. This care takes place every day; therefore His children bless Him and glorify Him every day.

68.16.2.en: 2- This verse ends with the word Selah, which is a musical pause for meditating on God's love and His care for us every day.

68.17.0.en: 20- He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death.

68.17.1.en: Our God is our Savior from all the afflictions of our life, even if they are hard, reaching to death. As Christ rose from the dead, so our God is able to raise us from afflictions, even if they bring us to the point of death. "The things which are impossible with men are possible with God" (Lk 18:27). Therefore we live in reassurance always, however many afflictions surround us.

68.18.0.en: 21- But God shall crush the head of his enemies, and the hairy scalp of such an one as goeth on still in his trespasses.

68.18.1.en: Scalp: the crown of the head.

68.18.3.en: If God cares for His children, at the same time He rejects evil and punishes it; whoever is proud and vain of his hair like Absalom awaits nothing but destruction, indeed God holds the wicked to account for every sin they commit, because He knows every sin, even if it is small like a hair. And whoever lifts up his head against God and lords it over others and wrongs them, God crushes all these heads that exalt themselves against Him.

68.19.0.en: 22- The Lord said, Return from Bashan, return from the depths of the sea: 23- That thy foot may be dipped in blood, the tongues of thy dogs have their portion from the enemies.

68.19.1.en: 1- God continues His discourse about His vengeance on the wicked who rebel against God; God seizes them even if they try to flee from Him, and climb the mountains, such as Mount Bashan, or flee into the depths of the sea; for He gathers them and gives His people victory over them, and the dogs lick up their blood, as the dogs licked the blood of Ahab and Jezebel. Thus the weak people of God trample their strong enemies, and their feet are dyed with the blood of the enemies, and it was an ancient custom in wars that the victor would dye his feet with the blood of the enemies. What is meant is that God gives His children victory, however weak they are, and however much their enemies exalt themselves against them.

68.19.2.en: 2- These two verses are a prophecy about Christ, who bound Satan by the cross, and passed through the winepress alone, and His garments were dyed with blood. Thus by shedding His blood on the cross He won a great victory over Satan.

68.20.0.en: 24- They have seen thy goings, O God, the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary. 25- The singers went before, the players on stringed instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels. 26- Bless ye God in the congregations, the Lord, ye that are from the fountain of Israel.

68.20.1.en: 1- When David brought the ark back from the house of Obed-edom the Gittite to Jerusalem he rejoiced greatly, and all the children of Israel rejoiced with him, and held fast to God's commandments and His ways, that they might live to God, and declared their submission to God that He might reign over their hearts. The singers from among the Levites and the maidens sang before the ark and played musical instruments, such as the stringed instruments and the timbrels, as they sang with timbrels after crossing the Red Sea.

68.20.2.en: 2- Then David calls on those who believe in God, who were refreshed with the waters of grace in the midst of the people of God, that is, from the fountain of Israel, to bless God and praise Him with a common praise.

68.20.3.en: 3- These verses are a prophecy about the Apostles and those who believe in Christ, who saw the life of Christ on earth and learned His ways and commandments, to shout and sing to God. And the Christians are those who came forth from the people of God the Jews, that is, from the fountain of Israel, because they are the new Israel. And even now the Church still praises God every day with songs of thanksgiving and glorification.

68.21.0.en: 27- There is little Benjamin, their ruler, the princes of Judah, all of them, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.

68.21.1.en: 1- David completes his discourse about the procession of joy and victory of the children of God, and mentions four of the tribes of the children of Israel; among them Benjamin, which was a small tribe, but from it came the first king of the children of Israel, Saul the son of Kish. Judah was a large tribe, and these two tribes dwelt side by side, and opposite them dwelt the two tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali. By this he means that all the tribes rejoiced in God's care and His work in them.

68.21.2.en: 2- From these four tribes came most of the disciples of Christ: from Benjamin came Paul, from Judah came Peter, Andrew, James and John, and most of the rest from Zebulun and Naphtali; that is, the Church with her Apostles rejoices in the work of God in her.

68.22.0.en: 28- Thy God hath commanded thy strength: strengthen, O God, that which thou hast wrought for us.

68.22.1.en: Thy strength: thy glory and thy power.

68.22.2.en: David reassures the people of God and says to them that God has commanded your strength, so do not be troubled by the power of the enemies and their threats; because your God, the Pantocrator, protects you, and has promised you glory and power, and therefore the people of God ask Him to support them in all their works that they may be blessed and prosper. And this is a prophecy about the preaching of the Apostles, as they ask God to strengthen them in it.

68.23.0.en: 29- Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents unto thee.

68.23.1.en: This verse is a clear prophecy about the faith of the Gentiles in Christ, as they come to the temple of the New Testament in Jerusalem, where Christ accomplished His redemption, for the temple is Christ, God incarnate, crucified for the world, and they declare their faith in Him, and even bring gifts, like the Magi, the kings of the East, who came with gifts for Christ. And every believer is a king over himself who offers his gift to Christ, which is his love and submission and obedience to His commandments.

68.24.0.en: 30- Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, till every one submit himself with pieces of silver: scatter thou the people that delight in war. 31- Princes shall come out of Egypt; Cush shall soon stretch out her hands unto God. Beast of the reeds: in the land of the Jews there grew a thicket, or reeds, in some marshes, in which beasts of prey dwelt. It may mean the crocodiles that live among the reeds in Egypt. What is meant by these beasts is the enemies of the children of Israel.

68.24.1.en: Herd of bulls: that is, a flock or gathering of bulls.

68.24.3.en: 1- David asks God to rebuke the enemies of His people who have savage natures, who are either the surrounding Gentiles, or the heretics present among the people of God, whom he expresses as the beast of the reeds. He also rebukes the herd of bulls, by which are meant those characterized by pride, that is, the proud enemies of the people of God who resist God. In addition to the calves of the peoples, that is, the peoples of the Gentiles who are led and submit to faith in Christ, and offer gifts such as silver. Silver also signifies redemption, that is, they seek Christ the Redeemer. Among these peoples are the great ones of the Egyptians who are distinguished by learning and honor, and likewise the people of Abyssinia who stretch out their hands and submit to the faith.

68.24.4.en: 2- David also asks God to scatter and drive away the peoples of the Gentiles who do not want to believe, so that He protects His people from them.

68.24.5.en: If only you would not resist God's commandments for the sake of your personal aims, but submit to Him and hold fast to them, then you will find your life, and rejoice in God's work in you; for He wants your salvation, and He must give you the joy of fellowship with Him, and grant you His treasures.

68.25.0.en: 32- Sing unto God, ye kingdoms of the earth; O sing praises unto the Lord; Selah.

68.25.1.en: 1- David calls on all the Gentiles to praise God, meaning those of the Gentiles who have believed in Christ, or who have heard about Christ. He calls them to believe, and then to praise God, declaring their joy in Him as a Lord to them who reigns over their hearts and lets them enjoy His care.

68.25.2.en: 2- The verse ends with the word "Selah," which is a musical pause for meditating on the greatness of God so that we may praise Him and glorify Him.

68.26.0.en: 33- To him that rideth upon the heavens of heavens, which were of old; lo, he doth send out his voice, and that a mighty voice.

68.26.1.en: 1- He describes God as reigning over the highest of the ancient heavens, that is, those He created at the beginning of creation. Here he points to the eternity of God, and that He is the Creator of all creation.

68.26.2.en: 2- He also speaks of the mighty voice of God, and this is not only through thunder and lightning and strong winds, but also through the mighty words of Christ, who rebuked the winds and the waves, cast out demons and raised Lazarus ... and likewise through His mighty word that terrifies sinners, as Paul spoke with Felix the governor about judgment and Felix trembled (Acts 24:25). This verse also points to the mighty voice of God on the day of judgment, when sinners tremble and the righteous rejoice.

68.27.0.en: 34- Ascribe ye strength unto God: his excellency is over Israel, and his strength is in the clouds.

68.27.1.en: 1- David also asks the Gentiles who have believed to glorify the great God, who is exalted above all gods, and whose greatness and majesty appear over His people Israel, so they glorify Him continually, and He protects them and subdues their enemies, as He struck the Egyptians with the ten plagues, and drowned Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea, and at the same time kept His people, and brought them across to the wilderness of Sinai, and freed them from slavery.

68.27.2.en: 2- God's power also appears in the cloud and mist rising in the sky with its beautiful white color, and this signifies His saints who live on earth a lofty, heavenly, luminous life.

68.28.0.en: 53- O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel is he that giveth strength and power unto his people. Blessed be God.

68.28.1.en: 1- David also speaks of the great fear of God in His holy places, which are the places of worship around the ark of the covenant of God in Jerusalem, and also the other parts of the tabernacle that were in Gibeon during David's life. And likewise the holy places are all the souls that have been sanctified to God and worshiped Him with all their heart, for He gives awe to His children in the eyes of others; because the world sees in them the power of God and the greatness of carrying out the commandment.

68.28.2.en: 2- God is the source of the people's strength, and therefore He protects His people who worship Him and subdues their enemies, so that His power appears in them, since they have no source of strength except God, and so they bless Him and praise Him continually.

68.28.3.en: Contemplate the greatness of God and the fear of Him so that your heart may be reassured, for He is your God who protects you, and at the same time reject every sin so as not to anger Him, and your heart will be purified and free to praise Him at all times.

68.28.4.en: God the Savior of the afflicted. To the Chief Musician upon Shoshannim. Of David. "Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul" (v. 1) Introduction:

68.28.7.en: When David was fleeing from the face of his son Absalom, then war broke out between them, and Absalom died, and before David returned to his throne. He was living and remembering his sufferings which he had passed through and was still suffering from, while a stranger to his throne in Jerusalem.

68.28.8.en: 3- This psalm is sung upon Shoshannim, which is:

68.28.10.en: b- A musical instrument resembling the lily flower.

68.28.11.en: 4- It is considered one of the Messianic psalms because it speaks clearly of the sufferings of Christ.

68.28.12.en: 5- This psalm resembles Psalm 22 in speaking of the sufferings of Christ.

68.28.13.en: 6- Many verses are quoted from this psalm in the New Testament; it is one of the psalms most quoted (Mt 27:35; Mk 15:24; Jn 15:25; Acts 1:20; Rom 15:3).

68.28.14.en: 7- Many parts of this psalm are prayed in the prayer for the departed in the prayer of the Third Hour.

68.28.15.en: 8- This psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.
